topic: Will the world's population keep growing indefinitely?
scientific_reframe: Under what jointly specified fertility, mortality, migration, and climate-disruption trajectories would global population continue increasing beyond 2100, and can a component-resolved, out-of-sample-calibrated ensemble distinguish those trajectories from trajectories that peak before 2100?
research_object: Country-by-age-by-sex population trajectories aggregated to global population, with demographic components and climate-disruption covariates represented separately.
primary_endpoint: Posterior probability that global population growth remains positive through 2100, together with the distribution of the first global peak year.

not_claimed: a causal estimate of climate change on fertility or mortality
a prediction of a single inevitable population total
policy recommendations derived from executed simulations

subhypotheses.question: How strongly do alternative country-level fertility convergence trajectories determine whether global growth persists beyond 2100?
How do longevity improvements and episodic mortality shocks change peak timing after conditioning on fertility?
When does migration redistribute age structure enough to change global peak timing, rather than only national trajectories?
Do explicitly uncertain climate-disruption covariates improve calibrated forecasts of demographic components beyond non-climate baselines?
Can a coherent cohort-component ensemble maintain calibration at country, regional, and global aggregation levels?
